Model fitted to the teacher expectancy studies

Source: R/data.R
raudenbush_fit.Rd

A fitted model for the 19 studies in raudenbush1985, as returned by bayes_efron_fit() with the default settings. It is thinned to 800 posterior draws, is used in vignette("teacher-expectancy"), and was created with

bayes_efron_fit(raudenbush1985, seed = 1985, thin = 15)

Usage

raudenbush_fit

Format

An object of class bef_fit_re; see bef_fit for its components and methods.

Source

Fitted with CmdStan 2.38.0 on 2026-10-10. The script is data-raw/example-fits.R in the source repository.

Details

Each of the 4 chains ran 1,000 warmup and 3,000 sampling iterations, and one draw out of every 15 was stored. Summaries are computed from the 800 stored draws, whereas the sampler diagnostics reported by diagnose() are computed from all 12,000. For these 19 studies the "pilot" method does not narrow the range, so the grid is the same as with grid_method = "paper_realdata". The object contains the draws of \(g\) but no site-level draws, and it can be used without CmdStan.

See also

raudenbush1985, bayes_efron_fit(), vignette("teacher-expectancy")

Examples

raudenbush_fit
#> <bayesEfron fit>
#> Model family: RE
#> Sites: 19
#> Grid method: pilot
#> Runtime: 0.6065 sec
#> Draws: 800 (4 chains, one iteration in 15 kept); site-level draws not kept
#> Diagnostics: Rhat 1.003; ESS bulk 994.5; ESS tail 1185; divergences 0; treedepth hits 0
#> Standard errors: 0.09381 to 0.373 (largest / smallest 3.976)
#> Grid: 101 points from -1.07 to 1.93; smallest standard error 3.127 grid spacings
#> Grid range: rule "pilot", not narrowed (the range of "paper_realdata"); point masses; 6 spline functions
#> Next: summary() and site_summary() for the sites, g_summary() for the distribution of effects, plot().
summary(raudenbush_fit)
